question_edited: What were the concerns about the structural integrity of the Eiffel Tower?
answer_edited: The Eiffel Tower's construction was paused halfway to the first level, necessitating a substantial timber scaffold, which raised concerns about the tower's structural integrity. This led to sensational headlines like "Eiffel Suicide!" and "Gustave Eiffel Has Gone Mad: He Has Been Confined in an Asylum" in the tabloid press. Several prominent artists of the time, including Charles Garnier and Alexander Dumas, expressed disapproval of the tower. Charles Garnier, for example, believed it was an "ugly blot on the Parisian landscape," while Dumas compared it to a "giant, rusty smokestack."

answer_edited: After some debate about the exact location of the tower, a contract was signed on 8 January 1887. Eiffel signed it acting in his own capacity rather than as the representative of his company, the contract granting him 1.5 million francs toward the construction costs: less than a quarter of the estimated 6.5 million francs. Eiffel was to receive all income from the tower for 20 years, after which it would revert to the city of Paris.

answer_edited: The Verkhovna Rada is the supreme legislative body of Ukraine, also known as the Ukrainian parliament.  It is composed of 450 members, elected by the people. In the 1990 Ukrainian parliamentary elections, candidates from the Democratic Bloc won landslide victories in western Ukrainian oblasts.  A majority of the seats had to hold run-off elections. On 18 March, Democratic candidates scored further victories in the run-offs.  The Democratic Bloc gained about 90 out of 450 seats in the new parliament.  On 6 April 1990, the Lviv City Council voted to return St. George Cathedral to the Ukrainian Greek Catholic Church.  The Russian Orthodox Church refused to yield.
